info.title: Functional Heritability Partitioning, Multi-Tissue Transcriptomic Colocalization, and Pharmacogenomic Target Deconvolution Across 127 Alzheimer's Disease Susceptibility Loci

text.text: Background: The landmark genome-wide association meta-analysis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and AD-by-proxy across N = 2, 815, 127 individuals (Uffelmann et al., Nature, 2026) expanded the known susceptibility landscape to 127 independent genomic risk loci (160 association signals) and established an autosomal common-variant SNP heritability of h 2 SNP = 16.0% on the liability scale.

Translating these 127 static statistical signals into pathway-stratified clinical trials requires resolving three quantitative gaps: how the non-APOE polygenic architecture partitions across distinct cellular programs, which effector genes operate via cortical parenchymal versus peripheral myeloid gene expression, and which targets possess nanomolar human bioactivity suitable for genetically stratified trials.

Methods: Operating entirely on individual-genotype-free summary statistics structured along a previously established tridimensional diagnostic framework (Axis 1: Etiology and Genetic Architecture; Axis 2: Molecular Pathophysiology and Biomarker Programs; Axis 3: Neuroanatomical-Cognitive Topography), we ingested the complete NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog build GCST90695466 (8, 159, 496 autosomal and 160, 704 X-chromosome variants).

First, we performed functional heritability partitioning via stratified excess χ 2 inflation (χ 2 -1) and additive genetic variance ( 2pqβ 2 ) across ±50 kb cis-regulatory windows of 50 fine-mapped effector genes organized into five mechanistic Axis 2 programs (MICROGLIAL_IMMUNE, PROTEOPATHY_AUTOPHAGY, ENDOCYTIC_VESICULAR, SYNAPTIC_CALCIUM, and MITOCHONDRIAL_OXIDATIVE).

Second, we conducted Summary-data-based Mendelian Randomization (SMR) and Approximate Bayes Factor colocalization (PP.H4) across 54 human tissues in GTEx v10 (4, 415 matched cis-eQTLs) alongside Open Targets v4 SuSiE fine-mapped credible sets spanning ROS/MAP dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), BrainSeq, primary human monocytes, and UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project (UKB-PPP) plasma pQTLs.

Third, we queried EMBL-EBI ChEMBL v34 across 2, 785 human bioactivity assays (IC 50 , K i , K d , EC 50 ) and Open Targets tractability matrices to construct an empirical pharmacogenomic target atlas.
Results: Across 8, 159, 496 autosomal variants, the genome-wide mean test statistic was χ 2 GW = 1.5099.

Outside the APOE/TOMM40 super-locus (max χ2 = 3, 267.15; 2pqβ2 = 0.0882, accounting for 74.82% of top-locus additive variance), 89, 589 cis-regulatory SNPs across 48 non-APOE effector genes exhibited a 12.88-fold heritability enrichment over the autosomal background.

Normalized across the 16.0% polygenic liability scale, non-APOE functional heritability concentrated in MICROGLIAL_IMMUNE (39.22% share; h 2 SNP = 6.28%; 13.02× enrichment; χ2 = 7.64) and PROTEOPATHY_AUTOPHAGY (36.34% share; h 2 SNP = 5.81%; 14.98× enrichment; χ2 = 8.64), followed by ENDOCYTIC_VESICULAR (16.71% share; h 2 SNP = 2.67%; 12.69× NOTE: This preprint reports new research that has not been certified by peer review and should not be used to guide clinical practice.
enrichment; χ2 = 7.47), SYNAPTIC_CALCIUM (5.40% share; h 2 SNP = 0.86%; 10.05× enrichment; χ2 = 6.13), and MITOCHONDRIAL_OXIDATIVE (2.33% share; h 2 SNP = 0.37%; 5.24× enrichment; χ2 = 3.67).

Multi-tissue SMR and colocalization resolved a striking divergence between Axis 3 cortical parenchyma and myeloid compartments: QPCT (rs2300880; Z SMR = -4.62, p SMR = 3.93 × 10 -6 , PP.H4 cis = 0.919, PP.H4 local = 0.994 in Brain_Cortex; PP.H4 local = 0.979 in Brain_Frontal_Cortex_BA9) and AXL (rs12979764; p SMR = 2.13 × 10 -4 , PP.H4 cis = 0.902, PP.H4 local = 0.924 in Brain_Cortex) colocalized directly within human cerebral cortex and ROS/MAP DLPFC.

Conversely, canonical myeloid and endocytic drivers (BIN1, CD33, TREM2, INPP5D, SYK ) exhibited near-zero bulk cortical eQTL colocalization (PP.H4 cis ≤ 0.025 in Brain_Cortex) despite high SuSiE Locus-to-Gene scores (L2G = 0.875-0.968) and robust colocalization in primary monocytes and spleen (INPP5D PP.H4 local = 0.992; BIN1 PP.H4 local = 0.999).

ChEMBL v34 bioactivity profiling confirmed low-nanomolar human target potency for clinical-stage compounds across all five programs, including isradipine (2.0 nM) and nilvadipine (19.0 nM) for CACNA1S, omaveloxolone (2.2 nM) for KEAP1, fostamatinib/R406 (41.0 nM) for SYK, and varoglutamstat/PQ912 (61.0 nM) for QPCT.
Conclusion: Over three-quarters (75.56%) of the non-APOE common-variant heritability of Alzheimer's disease resides within microglial immune surveillance and proteopathic clearance networks.

If prospectively validated in genotype-stratified clinical cohorts, these empirical summarystatistics findings suggest that therapeutic efficacy in sporadic AD may depend on matching pathway-selective drugs to a patient's individual Functional Pathway Burden Score rather than administering uniform monotherapies to genetically unstratified populations.
Alzheimer's disease (AD) has long been treated in the clinic as if its molecular etiology were uniform across patients who share an amnestic cognitive phenotype.
It is not.

While the histopathological hallmarks of extracellular amyloid-β (Aβ) plaques and intracellular hyperphosphorylated tau neurofibrillary tangles define the downstream neuropathological state, human genetics indicates that upstream entry into this cascade is governed by heterogeneous, semi-independent cellular failure modes [1] [2] [3].

text.text: Why do genetically supported targets repeatedly underperform in unstratified clinical trials?
A parsimonious explanation is pathway dilution.

If a specific biological mechanism-such as neuronal L-type calcium channel hyperexcitability or pyroglutamate-Aβ (pE3-Aβ) modification-accounts for only a modest fraction of polygenic liability across the broader AD population, or acts predominantly within a restricted cellular compartment, administering a pathway-specific inhibitor to an unselected cohort guarantees that most enrolled participants lack the corresponding genetic driver.
The recent publication of the largest AD genome-wide association meta-analysis to date by Uffelmann et al.

(Nature, 2026; preprint 2025) [3, 8], encompassing N = 2, 815, 127 individuals (138, 288 clinical AD cases, 111, 326 proxy cases, and 2, 565, 513 controls across 33 cohorts), expanded the susceptibility architecture of AD to 127 independent genomic risk loci (160 distinct association signals) and quantified the common-variant liability-scale heritability at h 2 SNP = 16.0%.

text.text: Five pharmacological insights emerged from the empirical ChEMBL v34 and Open Targets v4 deconvolution: 1.

Cortical-Colocalized Enzymatic Inhibition (QPCT ): Glutaminyl cyclase (CHEMBL4508; 273 human assays; target median IC50 = 62.0 nM, best assay 0.80 nM) catalyzes the formation of neurotoxic, degradation-resistant pyroglutamate-Aβ (pE3-Aβ).
Its oral clinical inhibitor varoglutamstat (CHEMBL3545085, PQ912; Phase IIb VIVIAD trial) [6] exhibits an empirical human IC50 = 61.0 nM (pIC50 = 7.21) and K i = 39.0 nM (pK i = 7.41).

Because QPCT is one of the rare AD loci that colocalizes directly with cortical gene expression (PP.H4 local = 0.994 in Brain_Cortex), our findings suggest that varoglutamstat trials should prospectively stratify participants by QPCT cis-eQTL genotype (rs2300880/rs1989172) and elevated CSF pE3-Aβ.

Myeloid Kinase and TAM Receptor Repurposing (SYK and AXL): Within the dominant MICROGLIAL_IMMUNE program (39.22% heritability share), spleen tyrosine kinase (SYK, CHEMBL2599; 500 assays; target median IC50 = 74.0 nM) acts directly downstream of TREM2 and Fcγ receptors to regulate microglial phagocytosis and NLRP3 inflammasome activation [21].

The FDA-approved oral prodrug fostamatinib (CHEMBL4802135, Phase IV) and its active metabolite R406 (CHEMBL186359) exhibit median human SYK inhibition of IC50 = 41.0 nM (pIC50 = 7.39, K d = 15.0 nM, best assay 0.68 nM).

Similarly, the corticalcolocalized TAM receptor tyrosine kinase AXL (CHEMBL4895; 500 assays) displays a target median IC50 = 44.0 nM (pIC50 = 7.36, best assay 0.03 nM), with clinical Phase II inhibitors (bemcentinib) and Phase IV multi-kinase agents (gilteritinib, cabozantinib) already characterized in humans.
However, Pillar 1 revealed that the entire SYNAPTIC_CALCIUM program accounts for only 5.40% of non-APOE heritability (h 2 SNP = 0.86%).
This quantitative mismatch provides a compelling genetic explanation for why the unstratified Phase III NILVAD trial (N = 511) [7] failed to meet its primary endpoint across an unselected AD cohort.

(Nature, 2026) [3] across GTEx v10 [11], Open Targets v4 SuSiE credible sets [15], and EMBL-EBI ChEMBL v34 [14], this study establishes three quantitative principles for precision neurology in sporadic Alzheimer's disease.
text.formatted: (Nature, 2026) <ref type="bibr" target="#b2">[3]</ref> across GTEx v10 <ref type="bibr" target="#b10">[11]</ref>, Open Targets v4 SuSiE credible sets <ref type="bibr" target="#b14">[15]</ref>, and EMBL-EBI ChEMBL v34 <ref type="bibr" target="#b13">[14]</ref>, this study establishes three quantitative principles for precision neurology in sporadic Alzheimer's disease.

text.text: First, our partitioned heritability analysis demonstrates that non-APOE polygenic susceptibility is neither uniformly distributed across the genome nor confined to classical amyloid precursor processing.

Instead, 75.56% of the partitioned common-variant heritability concentrates within two synergistic Axis 2 programs: microglial immune surveillance (MICROGLIAL_IMMUNE, 39.22% share, 13.02× enrichment) and proteopathic/autophagic clearance (PROTEOPATHY_AUTOPHAGY, 36.34% share, 14.98× enrichment), with endocytic-vesicular trafficking (ENDOCYTIC_VESICULAR, 16.71% share, 12.69× enrichment) forming a third structural bridge.
Together, these three clearance and neuroimmune programs account for 92.27% of the non-APOE polygenic liability (14.76% of the 16.0% total SNP heritability).
By contrast, synaptic calcium signaling (SYNAPTIC_CALCIUM, 5.40%) and mitochondrial oxidative stress (MITOCHONDRIAL_OXIDATIVE, 2.33%) account for only 7.73% combined.

We noted that this asymmetric distribution offers an immediate quantitative explanation for historical clinical trial failures: when a drug targeting a 2% to 5% heritability slice (such as nilvadipine targeting L-type calcium channels in NILVAD) [7] is tested in an unstratified AD population, statistical power to detect disease modification collapses unless enrollment is enriched for carriers of the corresponding pathway burden.

text.text: Second, our multi-tissue SMR and Bayesian colocalization results resolve an important paradox in functional neurogenomics.

Only a subset of AD risk loci-most notably QPCT (PP.H4 local = 0.994 in Brain_Cortex, PP.H4 local = 0.979 in Brain_Frontal_Cortex_BA9) and AXL (PP.H4 local = 0.924 in Brain_Cortex)-operate through cis-eQTLs that colocalize directly in bulk human cerebral cortex.

For the majority of microglial and endocytic drivers (BIN1, INPP5D, CD33, TREM2, SYK, PICALM ), bulk cortical eQTL colocalization is near zero (PP.H4 cis ≤ 0.025) because microglia constitute only 5% to 10% of parenchymal brain cells, causing their cell-type-specific enhancer and splicing signals to be masked by abundant neuronal and astrocytic transcripts in bulk cortical homogenates [20].

text.text: Integrating myeloid-enriched compartments (Whole_Blood, Spleen, primary human monocytes in Quach/Blueprint) and region-specific hippocampal eQTLs (BIN1 PP.H4 local = 0.847; ABCA7 PP.H4 local = 0.946) successfully recovered these causal regulatory links.
Within the tridimensional diagnostic framework [9], this finding reinforces the strict separation between Axis 2 cellular/molecular mechanisms and Axis 3 neuroanatomical topography.

text.text: Third, cross-referencing these colocalized targets against 2, 785 human bioactivity assays in ChEMBL v34 proves that actionable, low-nanomolar compounds already exist for each of the five Axis 2 biological programs.

If experimentally and clinically validated in prospective biomarker-and genotype-stratified cohorts, these summary-statistics observations would support a shift from singletarget empiricism toward pathway-matched combination therapy: pairing cortical pyroglutamate-Aβ inhibition (varoglutamstat, IC50 = 61.0 nM) or safely gated anti-amyloid antibodies with oral microglial SYK/TAM modulation (fostamatinib/R406, IC50 = 41.0 nM; bemcentinib, IC50 = 44.0 nM), while reserving dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (isradipine 2.0 nM, nilvadipine 19.0 nM) and Nrf2 activators (omaveloxolone 2.2 nM) for patients in the upper decile of synaptic or mitochondrial genetic burden.
Several limitations warrant consideration.

First, our partitioned heritability estimates rely on summary-level excess χ 2 and additive genetic variance ( 2pqβ 2 ) across ±50 kb cis-regulatory windows rather than individual-level LD matrices from the restricted N = 2.82M consortium cohorts; while highly concordant with S-LDSC expectations, distal trans-regulatory enhancers beyond 50 kb are only captured when linked via Open Targets SuSiE L2G credible sets.

Second, the Uffelmann et al. (2026) meta-analysis is predominantly composed of European-ancestry cohorts, meaning that allele frequencies and LD-block colocalization posteriors require dedicated validation across African, East Asian, and admixed populations.

Finally, in vitro nanomolar potency in ChEMBL v34 does not guarantee optimal blood-brain barrier penetration or target engagement in aging human brain parenchyma, underscoring the necessity of prospective Phase II/III clinical validation.
